records.source: הָיְתָ֣ה עָלַי֮ יַד־יְהוָה֒ וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נִי בְר֨וּחַ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְנִיחֵ֖נִי בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבִּקְעָ֑ה וְהִ֖יא מְלֵאָ֥ה עֲצָמֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: There was on me [the] hand of Yahweh, and he brought me out by [the] Spirit of Yahweh and set me down in the middle of the valley, and it [was] full of bones.
pieces: The hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} carried me out by the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and put me down in the middle of the valley. It was full of bones.

L.1: The hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was upon me, and by the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me out and set me down in the valley's midst; and it [was] full of bones.

R.1: The power of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me. By {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took me out and put me down in the middle of a valley. The valley was full of bones.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon me: the LORD's power took hold of me
decisions.reason: See 1:3. The phrase opens a new vision, as in 8:1 and 40:1.

decisions.choice: by the Spirit of the LORD: the LORD's Spirit carries Ezekiel
decisions.reason: As in 3:12-14; 8:3 and 11:1, 24, the Spirit lifts and carries Ezekiel in the vision (see 2:2). The word *ruach* will be used ten times in this passage, in its three senses: Spirit, breath and wind (see verse 5).

decisions.choice: the valley full of bones: a battlefield of the unburied dead
decisions.reason: The article ("the valley") may point to the plain where Ezekiel saw the glory in 3:22-23. The bones lie scattered and unburied, like those of an army killed in battle (verse 9, "these slain"). To be left unburied was a curse (Deuteronomy 28:26; Jeremiah 8:1-2).

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon me (L); came on me (B); the power of the LORD came on me (R); Spirit, capitalized
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula and for *ruach* where the Spirit lifts or carries Ezekiel (2:2). Readable names the LORD as the subject for clarity. The vision is narrative, so its dialogue takes double quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

records.heading: The valley of dry bones

records.source: וְהֶעֱבִירַ֥נִי עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם סָבִ֣יב׀סָבִ֑יב וְהִנֵּ֨ה רַבּ֤וֹת מְאֹד֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַבִּקְעָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה יְבֵשׁ֥וֹת מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And he made me pass by them all around, all around; and look, very many [were] on the face of the valley, and look, very dry.
pieces: He led me back and forth among them, and I saw that there were a great many of them on the floor of the valley, and they were very dry.

L.2: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led me around among them, all around; and look, [there were] very many on the surface of the valley, and look, [they were] very dry.

R.2: He led me all around among the bones. There were a great many of them on the ground in the valley, and they were very dry.

decisions.choice: very many and very dry: long dead, beyond all hope
decisions.reason: The bones have lain there a long time. Nothing in them suggests that life could return (verse 11). The word "very" is repeated to stress it.

decisions.choice: led me back and forth (B); all around (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "all around". Literal keeps "all around"; Balanced and Readable give its sense. Literal keeps "look" twice for the Hebrew *hinneh*, which marks what Ezekiel saw; Balanced says "I saw".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הֲתִחְיֶ֖ינָה הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֕ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אַתָּ֥ה יָדָֽעְתָּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, will these bones live? And I said, Lord Yahweh, you know.
pieces: He asked me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" I answered, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know."

L.3: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know."

R.3: He asked me, "Son of man, can these bones come back to life?" I answered, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know that."

decisions.choice: Lord GOD, you know: the answer leaves it to the LORD
decisions.reason: Ezekiel neither says yes nor no. By human reckoning the answer is no; only the LORD knows what he can do. The Hebrew stresses "you": you yourself know.

decisions.choice: will these bones live: can they come to life again
decisions.reason: The verb "live" runs through the passage (verses 5, 6, 9, 10, 14). The question is whether the dead can live.

decisions.choice: only you know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses "you" by adding the pronoun. Balanced and Readable say "only you" to carry the stress. "Lord GOD" is *Adonai YHWH*, as set for Ezekiel.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י הִנָּבֵ֖א עַל־הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם הָעֲצָמוֹת֙ הַיְבֵשׁ֔וֹת שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Prophesy over these bones and say to them, Dry bones, hear [the] word of Yahweh.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Prophesy over these bones and say to them, Dry bones, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

L.4: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Prophesy over these bones, and say to them, Dry bones, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Prophesy to these bones. Tell them, Dry bones, listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says!

decisions.choice: prophesy over these bones: the word of the LORD addressed to the dead
decisions.reason: Ezekiel is told to preach to corpses. It is the LORD's word, not the prophet's power, that will bring life (compare Genesis 1:3; Psalm 33:6).

decisions.choice: no inner quotation marks for the message
decisions.reason: By the rule set for Ezekiel, the message the prophet is told to deliver takes no quotation marks of its own, as in 11:5; the LORD's words to Ezekiel take double quotation marks because the vision is narrative. The LORD's speech runs to the end of verse 6.

records.source: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לָעֲצָמ֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנִ֜י מֵבִ֥יא בָכֶ֛ם ר֖וּחַ וִחְיִיתֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh to these bones: Look, I am bringing into you breath, and you will live.
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this to these bones: I am going to put breath into you, and you will come to life.

L.5: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} to these bones: Look, I am going to make breath enter you, and you will live.

R.5: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says to these bones: I am going to put breath into you, and you will come back to life.

decisions.choice: breath: *ruach*, one word for breath, wind and Spirit
decisions.reason: The Hebrew *ruach* means wind, breath and spirit, and verses 1-14 use all three senses of it. It is the Spirit of the LORD who carries Ezekiel (verse 1); breath that enters the bodies and makes them live (verses 5-6, 8-10); the four winds from which the breath is called (verse 9); and the LORD's own Spirit, which he will put in his people (verse 14). The passage plays on the one word: the breath that makes the bodies live comes from the winds and stands for the Spirit of God. The breath of life recalls Genesis 2:7, where God breathes into the man he has formed, and Psalm 104:29-30. Each verse states which sense it gives; the reader should know that behind all of them stands one Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: I will make breath enter you, and you will live: Genesis 2:7
decisions.reason: As God formed the man from dust and breathed into him the breath of life (Genesis 2:7), so here he first rebuilds the bodies (verses 6-8) and then gives them breath (verses 9-10). The restoration of Israel is pictured as a new creation.

decisions.choice: breath (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Here *ruach* is the breath of life that makes a body live, so every level says "breath" (m1). Readable says "come back to life" for "live", since the bones were dead. The formula follows 2:4.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּי֩ עֲלֵיכֶ֨ם גִּדִ֜ים וְֽהַעֲלֵתִ֧י עֲלֵיכֶ֣ם בָּשָׂ֗ר וְקָרַמְתִּ֤י עֲלֵיכֶם֙ ע֔וֹר וְנָתַתִּ֥י בָכֶ֛ם ר֖וּחַ וִחְיִיתֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will put on you sinews and bring up on you flesh and cover over you skin and put in you breath, and you will live; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: I will put tendons on you and make flesh grow on you and cover you with skin. I will put breath in you, and you will come alive. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.6: And I will put on you sinews, and I will bring up flesh on you, and I will overlay you with skin, and I will put in you breath, and you will live; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.6: I will put tendons on you. I will make muscles grow on you and cover you with skin. I will put breath in you, and you will come back to life. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: sinews: the tendons and ligaments that hold the body together
decisions.reason: The word means the cords that bind muscle to bone (Job 10:11). The bodies are rebuilt in order: sinews, flesh, skin, and last of all breath.

decisions.choice: sinews, flesh, skin, breath: Job 10:11
decisions.reason: Job describes his own making in the same order: "You clothed me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and sinews" (Job 10:11).

decisions.choice: breath; the refrain as settled
decisions.reason: *Ruach* is "breath" here, as in verse 5. The refrain follows the settled wording. Readable says "muscles" for "flesh", since the word means the body's flesh. The closing quotation mark ends the LORD's words to Ezekiel begun in verse 4.

records.source: וְנִבֵּ֖אתִי כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צֻוֵּ֑יתִי וַֽיְהִי־ק֤וֹל כְּהִנָּֽבְאִי֙ וְהִנֵּה־רַ֔עַשׁ וַתִּקְרְב֣וּ עֲצָמ֔וֹת עֶ֖צֶם אֶל־עַצְמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I prophesied as I was commanded; and there was a sound as I prophesied, and look, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone.
pieces: So I prophesied as I had been told. While I was prophesying, there was a noise, a rattling sound, and the bones came together, each bone to its own bone.

L.7: And I prophesied just as I had been commanded; and there was a sound as I prophesied, and look, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone.

R.7: So I did what I was told and prophesied. While I was speaking, I heard a noise, a loud rattling. The bones began to come together. Each bone joined the bone it belonged to.

decisions.choice: a rattling: a shaking, a clattering noise
decisions.reason: The word *ra'ash* means shaking or quaking, and it is used of earthquakes (38:19; Amos 1:1). Here it is the clatter of the bones coming together.

decisions.choice: I prophesied as I was commanded: Ezekiel's obedience
decisions.reason: The prophet does exactly what he is told (12:7; 24:18), and the LORD's word does what it says (Isaiah 55:10-11).

decisions.choice: a rattling (L, B); a loud rattling (R)
decisions.reason: Each level says "rattling" for the sound, not "earthquake", since the bones are the subject.

records.source: וְרָאִ֜יתִי וְהִנֵּֽה־עֲלֵיהֶ֤ם גִּדִים֙ וּבָשָׂ֣ר עָלָ֔ה וַיִּקְרַ֧ם עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם ע֖וֹר מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְר֖וּחַ אֵ֥ין בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I looked, and look, on them sinews, and flesh came up, and skin covered over them above; but breath there was none in them.
pieces: As I watched, tendons appeared on them, flesh grew on them, and skin covered them over. But there was no breath in them.

L.8: And I looked, and look, there were sinews on them, and flesh had come up, and skin had covered them over; but there was no breath in them.

R.8: As I watched, tendons and muscles grew on the bones, and skin covered them. But they were not breathing.

decisions.choice: there was no breath in them: bodies without life
decisions.reason: The bodies are whole, but they are still corpses. Rebuilding them is not enough; they need breath, the gift of life from God. The step echoes Genesis 2:7, where the man is formed before he receives the breath of life.

decisions.choice: breath (L, B); they were not breathing (R)
decisions.reason: *Ruach* is "breath" here, as in verses 5-6.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל־הָר֑וּחַ הִנָּבֵ֣א בֶן־אָ֠דָם וְאָמַרְתָּ֨אֶל־הָר֜וּחַ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה מֵאַרְבַּ֤ע רוּחוֹת֙ בֹּ֣אִי הָר֔וּחַ וּפְחִ֛י בַּהֲרוּגִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְיִֽחְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: From [the] four winds come, breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me, "Prophesy to the breath. Prophesy, son of man, and say to it, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Come from the four winds, breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live."

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and you will say to the breath, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: From the four winds come, breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live."

R.9: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, prophesy to the breath. Say to it, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Breath, come from the four winds! Breathe into these people who were killed, so that they may live again."

decisions.choice: the breath ... the four winds: the same word in two senses
decisions.reason: Ezekiel speaks to the *ruach* as breath and calls it from the four *ruchot*, the four winds, that is, from every direction (42:20; Daniel 8:8). The wind becomes breath for the bodies. The play prepares for verse 14, where the LORD says the life he gives is his own Spirit. Jesus uses the same play on wind and Spirit in John 3:8.

decisions.choice: these slain: people killed in battle
decisions.reason: The word means those who have been killed. The bones are the remains of a slaughtered people, Israel destroyed by war and exile (verse 11).

decisions.choice: breath (L, B, R); winds (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level says "breath" for the *ruach* that is addressed and "winds" for the four directions (m1). Literal says "breathe on", Balanced and Readable "breathe into". The message takes no quotation marks of its own, as in verse 4.

records.source: וְהִנַּבֵּ֖אתִי כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֑נִי וַתָּבוֹא֩ בָהֶ֨ם הָר֜וּחַ וַיִּֽחְי֗וּ וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ עַל־רַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם חַ֖יִל גָּד֥וֹל מְאֹד־מְאֹֽד׃ס
records.gloss: And I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army.
pieces: So I prophesied as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had commanded me, and breath entered them. They came to life and stood up on their feet, a huge army.

L.10: And I prophesied just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had commanded me, and into them came the breath, and they lived, and they stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army.

R.10: So I prophesied as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me to. Breath came into the bodies, and they came back to life. They stood up on their feet. There were so many of them that they were like a huge army.

decisions.choice: an army: a great host
decisions.reason: The word *chayil* means strength, and so an army. The dead have become a living host, a people again.

decisions.choice: they lived and stood on their feet: as Ezekiel himself was raised
decisions.reason: The Spirit set Ezekiel on his feet in 2:2 and 3:24. Now the people, too, are raised up. Revelation 11:11 uses the words of this verse for the two witnesses: "the breath of life from God entered into them, and they stood on their feet".

decisions.choice: breath (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: *Ruach* is "breath" here, as in verses 5-9. Readable adds "like" to make the picture plain.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, these bones, they [are] the whole house of Israel. Look, they are saying, Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are cut off.
pieces: He said to me, "Son of man, these bones stand for the whole house of Israel. They keep saying, 'Our bones have dried up, our hope is gone; we are completely cut off.'

L.11: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, these bones, they [are] the whole house of Israel. Look, they are saying, 'Dried up are our bones, and perished is our hope; we are cut off completely.'

R.11: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, these bones are all the people of Israel. They say, 'Our bones are dried up. We have no hope left. We are finished.'

decisions.choice: these bones are the whole house of Israel: the vision explained
decisions.reason: The vision is not about individual people raised from the dead but about the nation, dead in exile, which the LORD will bring back to life and to its land (verses 12-14). "The whole house of Israel" includes both kingdoms (verses 15-22).

decisions.choice: our bones are dried up; we are cut off: the exiles' despair
decisions.reason: The people speak as if they were dead already, with no strength and no future (compare Psalm 31:11; Proverbs 17:22; Lamentations 3:54). The vision takes their own words and answers them.

decisions.choice: cut off completely (L); completely cut off (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "for ourselves", which stresses the verb. The people's words are quoted inside the LORD's words, so they take single quotation marks inside the double ones.

records.source: לָכֵן֩ הִנָּבֵ֨א וְאָמַרְתָּ֜ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנֵּה֩ אֲנִ֨י פֹתֵ֜חַ אֶת־קִבְרֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם וְהַעֲלֵיתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִקִּבְרוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם עַמִּ֑י וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל־אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore prophesy and say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I am opening your graves, and I will bring you up from your graves, my people, and bring you into [the] land of Israel.
pieces: So prophesy and say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am going to open your graves and raise you up out of them, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. I will bring you into the land of Israel.

L.12: Therefore prophesy, and say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am going to open your graves and bring you up from your graves, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and bring you into the land of Israel.

R.12: So prophesy to them. Tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: My people, I am going to open your graves and bring you up out of them. I will bring you back to the land of Israel.

decisions.choice: I will open your graves: the return from exile pictured as resurrection
decisions.reason: The picture changes from bones in a valley to bodies in graves, but the meaning is the same: the LORD will bring his people back from the death of exile to their land. The passage does not set out a teaching about the resurrection of the body, but it shows the LORD as the one who can raise the dead, and later Scripture speaks of a bodily resurrection in similar words (Isaiah 26:19; Daniel 12:2; John 5:28-29).

decisions.choice: my people: the people the LORD still claims
decisions.reason: The LORD calls the despairing exiles "my people" (verse 13). His covenant with them is not over.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. The message takes no quotation marks of its own, as in verse 4. Readable starts a new sentence with "My people", where the pronoun is capitalized under either setting.

records.source: וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּפִתְחִ֣י אֶת־קִבְרֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם וּבְהַעֲלוֹתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִקִּבְרוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם עַמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And you will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I open your graves and when I bring you up from your graves, my people.
pieces: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, when I open your graves and raise you up out of them.

L.13: And you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I open up your graves and when I bring you up out of your graves, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

R.13: Then, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I open up your graves and lift you out of them.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD: the refrain, after rescue
decisions.reason: See 6:7. Here the people come to know the LORD through his power to give life.

decisions.choice: the refrain as settled
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֨י רוּחִ֤י בָכֶם֙ וִחְיִיתֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל־אַדְמַתְכֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֞ם כִּי־אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִׂ֖יתִי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live, and I will set you on your land; and you will know that I, Yahweh, have spoken and I will do [it], declares Yahweh.
pieces: I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit within you so that you live, and I will set you down on your own soil. Then you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken and will act, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.14: And I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit within you, and you will live, and I will place you on your own soil; and you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken and will do [it], declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.14: I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit in you, and you will live. I will let you live in your own country. Then you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have said this and will do it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: my Spirit: the LORD's own Spirit, the source of the people's new life
decisions.reason: The *ruach* that was breath in verses 5-10 is now named as the LORD's own Spirit. The same promise is given in 36:27 and 39:29. The people's new life is not their own strength but God's Spirit in them.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD: the name alone
decisions.reason: The formula here has the divine name alone, not "the Lord GOD", as in a few other places in the book.

decisions.choice: Spirit, capitalized; I, the LORD, have spoken; declares (L, B) / says (R) the LORD
decisions.reason: Here *ruach* is the LORD's own Spirit, capitalized by Isaiah's rule as at 2:2. "I, the LORD, have spoken" and *ne'um* follow the settled wording. The closing quotation mark ends the LORD's words begun in verse 9.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.15: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: the sign of the two sticks
decisions.reason: A new message, with a sign Ezekiel acts out (as in chapters 4-5 and 12): two sticks joined in his hand, showing that Israel and Judah will be one nation again.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. What follows is the LORD's message, which takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

records.heading: Two sticks become one

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם קַח־לְךָ֙ עֵ֣ץ אֶחָ֔ד וּכְתֹ֤ב עָלָיו֙ לִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְלִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חֲבֵרָ֑יו וּלְקַח֙ עֵ֣ץ אֶחָ֔ד וּכְת֣וֹב עָלָ֗יו לְיוֹסֵף֙ עֵ֣ץ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְכָל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חֲבֵרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, take for yourself one stick and write on it, For Judah and for [the] sons of Israel his companions; and take one stick and write on it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all [the] house of Israel his companions.
pieces: Now you, son of man, take a stick of wood and inscribe it, "For Judah and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} allied with him." Then take a second stick and inscribe it, "For Joseph, that is, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel allied with him."

L.16: And you, son of man, take for yourself a single stick and inscribe on it, "For Judah and for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel associated with him"; then take another stick and inscribe on it, "For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all the house of Israel associated with him."

R.16: Son of man, take a stick and write on it, "This belongs to Judah and the people of Israel who are joined to it." Then take another stick and write on it, "This belongs to Joseph, that is, Ephraim, and all the people of Israel who are joined to it."

decisions.choice: Judah and Joseph, the stick of Ephraim: the southern and the northern kingdoms
decisions.reason: After Solomon the people split into two kingdoms: Judah in the south, with Jerusalem, and Israel in the north, often called Ephraim after its largest tribe, which descended from Joseph (1 Kings 12). The northern kingdom was taken into exile by Assyria in 722 BC, and Judah by Babylon in 597-586 BC.

decisions.choice: a stick: a piece of wood
decisions.reason: The word *'ets* means wood, a stick or a staff. It may be a plain stick, or a wooden writing board. Numbers 17:16-26 tells of a staff for each tribe with its name written on it.

decisions.choice: his companions: the tribes joined to him
decisions.reason: Judah was joined by Benjamin and by people from other tribes who came south (2 Chronicles 11:12-17); Ephraim stood for the other northern tribes.

decisions.choice: stick (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level says "stick", the plainest word for the object (m2). The words written on the sticks take double quotation marks, as text quoted inside the LORD's message. Literal says "associated with him" for "his companions"; Readable says "joined to it".

records.source: וְקָרַ֨ב אֹתָ֜ם אֶחָ֧ד אֶל־אֶחָ֛ד לְךָ֖ לְעֵ֣ץ אֶחָ֑ד וְהָי֥וּ לַאֲחָדִ֖ים בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And join them one to another for yourself into one stick, and they will become one in your hand.
pieces: Join the two to each other to make one stick, so that they are one in your hand.

L.17: And join them one to the other into one stick, so that they become one in your hand.

R.17: Then hold them together so that they look like one stick in your hand.

decisions.choice: one in your hand: the sign of the united people
decisions.reason: The two sticks held as one show what the LORD will do (verse 19). The sign is explained when the people ask about it (verses 18-19).

decisions.choice: hold them together (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring near. It is not said how the sticks were joined; Readable says Ezekiel holds them so that they look like one.

records.source: וְכַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ יֹאמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ בְּנֵ֥י עַמְּךָ֖ לֵאמֹ֑ר הֲלֽוֹא־תַגִּ֥יד לָ֖נוּ מָה־אֵ֥לֶּה לָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And when the sons of your people say to you, saying, Will you not tell us what these [are] to you?
pieces: When your own people ask you, "Will you not tell us what you mean by this?"

L.18: And when the {{gender:children|sons}} of your people say to you, "Will you not tell us what you mean by these?"

R.18: Your people will ask you, "Tell us what this means."

decisions.choice: will you not tell us what these mean to you: the sign invites a question
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's signs were meant to make the people ask (12:9; 24:19). The answer follows in verse 19.

decisions.choice: your own people (B); your people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 3:11 and 33:2. The people's words take double quotation marks.

records.source: דַּבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנֵּה֩ אֲנִ֨י לֹקֵ֜חַ אֶת־עֵ֤ץ יוֹסֵף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיַד־אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְשִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חֲבֵרָ֑יו וְנָתַתִּי֩ אוֹתָ֨ם עָלָ֜יו אֶת־עֵ֣ץ יְהוּדָ֗ה וַֽעֲשִׂיתִם֙ לְעֵ֣ץ אֶחָ֔ד וְהָי֥וּ אֶחָ֖ד בְּיָדִֽי׃
records.gloss: Speak to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I am taking the stick of Joseph, which [is] in [the] hand of Ephraim, and [the] tribes of Israel his companions, and I will put them with it, [with] the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they will be one in my hand.
pieces: tell them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim's hand, and of the tribes of Israel associated with him, and join it to the stick of Judah. I will make them a single stick, and they will become one in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.

L.19: say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which [is] in Ephraim's hand, and the tribes of Israel, his associates, and I will set them upon it, [upon] the stick of Judah, and I will make them into one stick, and they will be one in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.

R.19: Then tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which Ephraim holds, and of the tribes of Israel joined to it. I will join it to the stick of Judah and make them one stick. They will be one in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.

decisions.choice: one in my hand: the LORD makes the two peoples one
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel's hand the sticks are a sign; in the LORD's hand they become one in fact. The split of 1 Kings 12 will be healed.

decisions.choice: I will put them with it, with the stick of Judah: the Hebrew is awkward
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "I will put them on it, the stick of Judah". The sense is plain: the northern tribes will be joined to Judah.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Verse 19 begins with "Speak to them" and completes the sentence of verse 18, so it starts with a small letter at Literal and Balanced. The message takes no quotation marks of its own.

records.source: וְהָי֨וּ הָעֵצִ֜ים אֲֽשֶׁר־תִּכְתֹּ֧ב עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם בְּיָדְךָ֖ לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And the sticks on which you write will be in your hand before their eyes,
pieces: Hold the sticks you have written on in your hand where they can see them,

L.20: And the sticks on which you write shall be in your hand before their eyes,

R.20: Hold the sticks you wrote on in your hand where the people can see them.

decisions.choice: in your hand before their eyes: the sign is shown as the words are spoken
decisions.reason: The sign is held up while Ezekiel speaks the words of verses 21-28.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on (L, B)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 21, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

records.source: וְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנִ֤י לֹקֵ֨חַ֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִבֵּ֥ין הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָֽלְכוּ־שָׁ֑ם וְקִבַּצְתִּ֤י אֹתָם֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אוֹתָ֖ם אֶל־אַדְמָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: and speak to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I am taking [the] sons of Israel from among the nations where they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them to their land.
pieces: and say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am going to take the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from all around and bring them back to their own land.

L.21: and say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am going to take the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from among the nations to which they have gone, and gather them from every side, and bring them to their own soil.

R.21: Then tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to take the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from all around and bring them home to their own land.

decisions.choice: I will take, gather and bring them: as 36:24
decisions.reason: The promise repeats 11:17; 34:13 and 36:24, here for both kingdoms.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. "The sons of Israel" follows the settled wording: "children" (L) and "Israelites" (B, R) through the gender setting.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֣יתִי אֹ֠תָם לְג֨וֹי אֶחָ֤ד בָּאָ֨רֶץ֙ בְּהָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמֶ֧לֶךְ אֶחָ֛ד יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לְכֻלָּ֖ם לְמֶ֑לֶךְ וְלֹ֤א יִֽהְיוּ־עוֹד֙ לִשְׁנֵ֣י גוֹיִ֔ם וְלֹ֨א יֵחָ֥צוּ ע֛וֹד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י מַמְלָכ֖וֹת עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And I will make them one nation in the land, on [the] mountains of Israel, and one king will be king for all of them; and they will no longer be two nations, and they will no longer be divided again into two kingdoms.
pieces: I will make them into a single nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, with one king ruling over them all. Never again will they be two nations or be split into two kingdoms.

L.22: And I will make them into one nation in the land, on Israel's mountains, and one king will be king for all of them; and they will no longer be two nations, and no longer be divided into two kingdoms.

R.22: In the land, on the mountains of Israel, I will make them one nation. They will all have one king. They will never again be two nations or be divided into two kingdoms.

decisions.choice: one nation, one king: the end of the division
decisions.reason: The two kingdoms had been divided since about 930 BC, and the north had been in exile for well over a century. The LORD promises to make them one again under one king (Hosea 2:2; Jeremiah 3:18).

decisions.choice: king: *melekh*
decisions.reason: Here the coming ruler is called "king", the usual word; in verses 24-25 he is called king and prince (see 34:24).

decisions.choice: king (L, B); rule (R)
decisions.reason: The word *melekh* is "king" at every level; Readable says "one king will rule" for "one king will be king".

records.source: וְלֹ֧א יִֽטַמְּא֣וּ ע֗וֹד בְּגִלּֽוּלֵיהֶם֙ וּבְשִׁקּ֣וּצֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְכֹ֖ל פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֑ם וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּ֣י אֹתָ֗ם מִכֹּ֤ל מוֹשְׁבֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטְא֣וּ בָהֶ֔ם וְטִהַרְתִּ֤י אוֹתָם֙ וְהָיוּ־לִ֣י לְעָ֔ם וַאֲנִ֕י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they will no longer defile themselves with their idols and with their detestable things and with all their transgressions; and I will save them from all their dwelling places in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them; and they will be my people, and I will be their God.
pieces: They will no longer make themselves unclean with their idols, their vile idols or any of their rebellious acts. I will rescue them from all the places where they lived and sinned, and I will make them clean. They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

L.23: And they will no longer defile themselves with their filthy idols and their detestable things and all their transgressions; and I will save them from all their dwelling places in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them; and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

R.23: They will no longer make themselves unclean by worshiping their idols and their disgusting idols or by any of their other sins. I will save them from all the places where they lived and sinned, and I will make them clean. They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

decisions.choice: their dwelling places: possibly "their backslidings"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "all their dwelling places in which they sinned". With a small change in two letters, the word reads "their turnings away", that is, their unfaithfulness, and the Septuagint seems to read it so. The standard Hebrew text is kept: the LORD will save them from the places where they sinned.

decisions.choice: they will be my people, and I will be their God: the covenant formula
filthy idols, detestable things, transgressions (L); idols, vile idols, rebellious acts (B); idols, disgusting idols, sins (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *gillulim*, *shiqqutsim* and *pesha'* in Ezekiel.

records.source: וְעַבְדִּ֤י דָוִד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְרוֹעֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד יִהְיֶ֣ה לְכֻלָּ֑ם וּבְמִשְׁפָּטַ֣י יֵלֵ֔כוּ וְחֻקֹּתַ֥י יִשְׁמְר֖וּ וְעָשׂ֥וּ אוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And my servant David [will be] king over them, and one shepherd will be for all of them; and in my judgments they will walk, and my statutes they will keep and do them.
pieces: My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings and be careful to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes.

L.24: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David [will be] king over them, and one shepherd there will be for all of them; and they will walk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and do them.

R.24: A king from the family of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will rule over them. All of them will have one shepherd. They will live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules and carefully obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws.

decisions.choice: my servant David, king, one shepherd: 34:23-24
decisions.reason: See 34:23. Here the coming David is called "king" (*melekh*) as well as shepherd; in verse 25 he is "prince". Under him the people will at last keep the LORD's law, as 36:27 promised.

decisions.choice: servant; judgments, statutes (L); rulings, statutes (B); rules, laws (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *'eved* (34:23) and for the LORD's commands in Ezekiel. Readable says "a king from the family of" as in 34:23. Balanced begins the sentence with "My", where the pronoun is capitalized under either setting.

records.source: וְיָשְׁב֣וּ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָתַ֨תִּי֙ לְעַבְדִּ֣י לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָֽשְׁבוּ־בָ֖הּ אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְיָשְׁב֣וּ עָלֶ֡יהָ הֵ֠מָּה וּבְנֵיהֶ֞ם וּבְנֵ֤י בְנֵיהֶם֙ עַד־עוֹלָ֔ם וְדָוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י נָשִׂ֥יא לָהֶ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they will dwell on the land that I gave to my servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt; and they will dwell on it, they and their sons and their sons' sons forever; and David my servant [will be] prince for them forever.
pieces: They will live in the land I gave to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, the land where your ancestors lived. They will live there forever, they and their children and their grandchildren, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will be their prince forever.

L.25: And they will dwell in the land that I gave to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt; and they will dwell in it, they and their {{gender:children|sons}} and their {{gender:children's children|sons' sons}} forever; and David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant [will be] their prince forever.

R.25: They will live in the land I gave to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, where your ancestors lived. They and their children and grandchildren will live there forever. And the king from the family of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will be their ruler forever.

decisions.choice: prince: see 34:24
decisions.reason: The ruler is called *nasi'*, "prince", as in 34:24 and chapters 44-48.

decisions.choice: forever: a lasting kingdom
decisions.reason: The promise recalls the LORD's promise to David that his throne would stand forever (2 Samuel 7:13-16; Psalm 89:4-5). Luke 1:32-33 speaks of Jesus' reign in these terms.

decisions.choice: servant (L, B, R); prince (L, B); ruler (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *'eved* and *nasi'*. "Children" and "children's children" take the gender setting at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "children and grandchildren".

records.source: וְכָרַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ בְּרִ֣ית שָׁל֔וֹם בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם יִהְיֶ֣ה אוֹתָ֑ם וּנְתַתִּים֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אוֹתָ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֧י אֶת־מִקְדָּשִׁ֛י בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will make for them a covenant of peace; an everlasting covenant it will be with them; and I will give them and multiply them, and I will set my sanctuary in their midst forever.
pieces: I will make a covenant of peace with them, a covenant that will last forever. I will establish them and make them numerous, and I will place {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary among them forever.

L.26: And I will make for them a covenant of peace; a covenant of perpetuity it will be with them; and I will establish them and increase them, and I will place {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary in their midst forever.

R.26: I will make a peace agreement with them that will last forever. I will settle them in the land and make them grow in number. I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple among them forever.

decisions.choice: a covenant of peace, an everlasting covenant: 34:25 and 16:60
decisions.reason: The covenant of peace of 34:25 is called "everlasting", as in 16:60 and Isaiah 55:3; 61:8.

decisions.choice: I will give them: the sense is uncertain
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "I will give them". It may mean "I will establish them" or "I will set them [in their land]". The Septuagint does not have these words.

decisions.choice: my sanctuary in their midst forever: the LORD's presence among his people
decisions.reason: The sanctuary that the glory left (10:18-19; 11:22-23) will be set among the people forever. Chapters 40-48 describe it.

decisions.choice: a peace agreement (R); temple (R)
decisions.reason: As at 34:25, Readable says "agreement" for "covenant", and "temple" for "sanctuary", as at 11:16.

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה מִשְׁכָּנִי֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָיִ֥יתִי לָהֶ֖ם לֵֽאלֹהִ֑ים וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ־לִ֥י לְעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And my dwelling place will be over them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people.
pieces: My dwelling place will be among them, and I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

L.27: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dwelling place will be with them; and I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

R.27: I will live among them, and I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

decisions.choice: my dwelling place will be with them: the LORD will live among them
decisions.reason: The word *mishkan* is the word used for the tabernacle, the tent where the LORD lived among Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 25:8-9). The preposition can mean "over" or "with"; the sense is that the LORD's presence will rest among and over his people.

decisions.choice: my dwelling place with them; I will be their God: 2 Corinthians 6:16 and Revelation 21:3
decisions.reason: Paul quotes these words, joined with Leviticus 26:11-12, to say that the church is the temple of the living God (2 Corinthians 6:16). Revelation 21:3 uses them of the new creation: "the dwelling of God is with human beings". John 1:14 says that the Word "tabernacled among us".

decisions.choice: dwelling place ... with them (L, B); I will live with them (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "with them" for the preposition, which fits both senses (m1). Readable says plainly what the dwelling place means. Balanced begins with "My", capitalized under either setting.

records.source: וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בִּהְי֧וֹת מִקְדָּשִׁ֛י בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And the nations will know that I, Yahweh, sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary is in their midst forever.
pieces: Then the nations will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, make Israel holy, when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary is among them forever.

L.28: And the nations will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, make Israel holy, when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary is in their midst forever.

R.28: Then the nations will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have made Israel holy, because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple will be among them forever.

decisions.choice: I, the LORD, sanctify Israel: Leviticus 20:8
decisions.reason: The words are those of the holiness laws: "I am the LORD who makes you holy" (Leviticus 20:8; 22:32). The LORD's presence among his people sets them apart as his.

decisions.choice: make holy (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb *qadash* means to make holy, to set apart. Each level says "make holy", so that the link with "sanctuary" (holy place) is kept in sense.
